doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Favorites on the radio: Bob Zurke and the Bob Crosby band
summary: Sherman names Bob Zurke, the Crosby band at the Black Hawk and Teddy Wilson as early piano favorites; a coffee pause interrupts.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Who were some of your favorites in those radio days to listen to?
I was just thinking about that. Well it’s funny, in those days — well I guess, well Bob Zurke probably was the first piano player, with the Bob Crosby band.
Okay. Help my throat a little.
They say warm stuff is good for your throat.
Yeah. We were talking about Bob Zurke actually.

Yeah, listening, as you say, starting to listen to the radio and hear the bands that I like, and getting to the age where it was really, gee, I want to listen to that. Say ‘35, ‘6. I think the Bob Crosby band from the Black Hawk. I think — who did they — they followed Coon-Sanders I think was in there before, who didn’t impress me too much. But the Bob Crosby band, and then hearing Bob Zurke. I was very impressed with him. And of course on records Teddy Wilson I guess was the next.
